newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Tuesday boosted by the large number of new domestic A share issues scheduled for the next few days, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 10.35 percent from 8.02 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 6.5 million lots from 10.7 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
About a dozen firms will issue or list A shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges this week.
"The new issues have created a bulge in short-term money demand on the repo market," said one trader. "Institutions have borrowed heavily, especially the early-maturing contracts."
The strong performance of the A share markets in the past two days was another factor in Tuesday's rise, traders said.
Traders said they expected the repo rates to continue to move at the current high level in the next few days.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed in slow trading on Tuesday despite their high yields with many investors cashing in their positions to trade on the booming stock markets, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 121.04 yuan from 120.94 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 1.1 million lots from 827,336 lots but was still very thin, traders said.
Traders said the spot market would be left in the cold if the stock markets resumed their bull run.
